title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Crescent Logistics
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on contract extension, adding EU region capacity, and bumping Dedicated GPU pool by 2x. Customer requested updated pricing, SOC2/KMS confirmations and a performance benchmark in EU region before committing to 12-month extension.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated quote with 12-month extension + 2x Dedicated capacity and EU region pricing by 2026-08-14
Lina to schedule an EU-region micro-benchmark (throughput + p95 latency) for customer workload week of 2026-08-18
Jordan to share SOC2 report and KMS integration docs by 2026-08-13
Customer to confirm internal budget and procurement timeline by 2026-08-20
action_items: Lina Gomez | Run EU micro-benchmark and share results | 2026-08-21
Samir Patel | Prepare and send updated quote with tiered pricing and commitment options | 2026-08-14
Jordan Kim | Provide SOC2 and KMS/HSM documentation + network/VPC checklist | 2026-08-13
Priya Shah | Share procurement timeline and required PO format | 2026-08-20
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-12 15:00 PDT | Duration: 49m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM); Rachel (Crescent VP Eng), Tom (Head of ML), Priya (Procurement), Marco (SRE)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — you see the same list, Rachel?
[00:08] Rachel: Yep, all good. Thanks Samir. We wanted to keep this focused on renewal and the capacity expansion we talked about in the email.
[00:15] Samir: Perfect. Quick agenda: one, renewal length and pricing options; two, Dedicated capacity bump and EU region add; three, security and procurement asks; four, next steps. Lina will run through the technical asks and then we can talk numbers.
[00:29] Tom: Sounds great. From our side, main things are: we want the additional throughput for peak routing and we want the EU region for GDPR compliance on some customer workloads. Also curious about fallback behavior if EU capacity is constrained.
[00:43] Lina: Sure — so for Dedicated we recommend scaling the GPU pool from the current 4x to 8x for peak windows; autoscale remains, but we can reserve burst capacity. For EU region we can provision a separate dedicated pool in eu-west-1, same config, and route based on region tag. Fallback policy can optionally route to hosted low-latency nodes but that would need PKIs and data residency discussions.
[01:05] Marco: Just to clarify, if we route to hosted nodes, does that mean data leaves EU? We need to avoid that for EU-regulated customers.
[01:12] Lina: Good callout. We would not route cross-region by default — policy is configurable. If you choose strict residency, fallback would instead queue or scale more aggressively in region.
[01:23] Rachel: Ok that helps. Priya, from procurement, we need pricing scenarios with committed versus burst options. Also, a 12-month contract would be preferable for budget reasons if the unit price is right.
[01:35] Priya: And we need SOC2 docs and confirmation on KMS/HSM support. Also if there's any vendor onboarding form we need to fill, send it over.
[01:44] Jordan: We'll get SOC2 and the KMS integration note — Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS and we have HSM options for Private deployments. I can share the compliance pack after the call.
[01:55] Samir: On pricing, we have three options: month-to-month (current), 12-month committed with a discount, and 24-month with deeper discount + committed burst pool. For this call I'll give ballpark numbers and send formal quote.
[02:07] Tom: For the micro-benchmark — our critical metric is p95 latency under a mixed sequence distribution ~ 300 tokens, 3 concurrent requests per connection, and throughput spikes to 200 reqs/s during peaks.
[02:20] Lina: That's helpful — we'll reproduce that pattern in the EU micro-benchmark. Any specific models/quantization profiles you're using?
[02:27] Tom: We're on a trimmed open model, 8-bit quant, and some KV cache reuse. We saw some token stalls earlier which we think might be kernel selection or batching configuration on your side.
[02:38] Lina: We noted a similar thing last quarter — likely a batching window mismatch and KV cache warm start. For the benchmark we'll run with your exact model artifact and config; if you can share a lightweight sample or docker tag, that'd speed things.
[02:51] Rachel: We'll share an anonymized sample payload plus config.
[02:55] Priya: Quick procurement question — do you require a signed MSA for a 12-month? Or can we do PO with terms?
[03:03] Samir: We can do a PO referencing our Master Service Agreement; if legal needs changes we can iterate. For enterprise accounts we typically do an MSA, but it's flexible.
[03:12] Priya: Ok noted.
[05:10] (conversation continues; jumping ahead to technical deep-dive)
[05:12] Lina: One more thing on fallback — the platform supports model variants so you can set a cheaper quantized fallback in case of capacity constraints; quality tradeoff is visible in evals.
[05:25] Tom: Would that be automated or something we control?
[05:29] Lina: You control it. Routing policies can be by latency objective, cost cap, or explicit region. So if EU can't handle, you can either fail fast, fallback to a compatible quantized variant in-region, or route to a different region if your compliance allows.
[05:45] Marco: We'll want the in-region fallback only. No cross-border routing without consent.
[05:52] Samir: Totally understood. We'll include strict residency configuration in the quote as an option.
[06:10] Rachel: Pricing — can you give a rough delta for 2x Dedicated capacity and adding EU region?
[06:16] Samir: Ballpark numbers: 2x Dedicated pool increases committed spend roughly 1.9x due to reserved discount; adding EU region has a region premium about 10-12% for dedicated hardware. If you add 12-month commitment, we can layer a 15% discount on top. Exact numbers on the formal quote.
[06:33] Priya: And what about overage? If we exceed reserved capacity during a month, how are bursts billed?
[06:39] Samir: Bursts are billed at a predefined burst rate which is higher than reserved but still capped. We can set a monthly cap with alerting.
[07:00] (small crosstalk)
[07:05] Tom: On latency, in our prod runs we saw p95 ~420ms for 300 tokens — any way to get that under 300ms?
[07:12] Lina: Two levers: 1) move to a larger instance type for lower kernel overhead; 2) tune batching window and increase KV cache locality. We'll test both during the benchmark. Also, quantization profile can help — 8-bit is often fine but some models benefit from specialized quant kernels.
[07:30] Tom: Good. Can you also surface per-token cost breakdowns by route? We want to attribute costs to features.
[07:37] Jordan: In Redwood Console you get token-level cost and latency breakdown per route/model. We'll include screenshots and a short guide with the quote.
[07:44] Rachel: Regarding security: SOC2 is a blocker for Finance customers. Also our legal wants confirmation of audit logging retention period and SSO/SAML support.
[07:52] Jordan: SOC2 will be provided. Audit logs retention configurable; default is 90 days, enterprise retention add-on available. SSO/SAML and SCIM are supported.
[08:00] Priya: KMS vendor support? We use AWS KMS.
[08:03] Jordan: We support AWS KMS for customer-managed keys and have HSM integrations for Private. We'll send the integration notes.
[08:12] Rachel: Great. Timeline-wise, if we get benchmark results and the security pack by the 21st, can procurement sign by end of month?
[08:20] Priya: That's aggressive but possible if numbers look good. We need the PO template and quote in the right format.
[08:26] Samir: We'll aim to get docs earlier — SOC2 + KMS by 2026-08-13, quote by 2026-08-14, benchmark results by 2026-08-21.
[08:35] (silence, notes being taken)
[20:10] (mid call, deeper technical notes — paraphrased)
[20:15] Lina: Regarding kernel selection, we can force a particular execution path during the benchmark to match your production artifact; that avoids token stalls from dynamic kernel switching.
[20:28] Tom: That would be ideal. Also, can we test cache warm starts? We often see cold-kv penalty in morning spikes.
[20:36] Lina: We'll script a warmup sequence to mimic morning traffic so we can observe warm-start behavior and recommend pre-warm policies.
[20:45] Marco: Also, does Redwood expose tracing hooks so our SREs can correlate spans?
[20:51] Jordan: Yes — there are tracing hooks and per-request IDs; we can integrate with your existing tracing backend.
[21:00] Tom: Good.
[34:45] (procurement segment)
[34:50] Priya: For billing, we need monthly invoices with a line item for reserved capacity and a separate line for bursts/overage. Also requirement for PO number on invoice.
[34:58] Samir: We'll format invoices that way and include the PO field.
[35:05] Priya: Also include data residency clause in the MSA addendum.
[35:10] Jordan: We have a standard addendum for data residency and VPC requirements; we'll attach that.
[44:00] (recap and close)
[44:05] Samir: Recap: 1) We'll send updated quote with options (12-mo, 24-mo, and PO-first flow). 2) Lina to run EU micro-benchmark with your payloads and share results. 3) Jordan to send SOC2/KMS/HSM docs and network/VPC checklist. 4) Priya will confirm procurement timeline. Any objections?
[44:25] Rachel: No objections. Sounds good.
[44:28] Priya: One last ask — can the quote show tiered pricing by token volume and committed burst buckets?
[44:33] Samir: Yes, we'll include tiered pricing and sample billing scenarios.
[44:38] Tom: Also add a note about rollback policies for model rollouts — if a new model regresses, can we auto-fallback to previous model?
[44:45] Lina: Yes — Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic rollback to pinned versions; we'll include the rollout options doc.
[44:55] Samir: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up and schedule the benchmark.
[48:30] Rachel: Thanks all.
[48:35] Meeting ended.
